title: Student Accommodation Form
transcript:
Speaker 1: Officer: Good morning. Can I help you?
Speaker 2: Student: Yes. I’ve just been accepted on a course at the university, and I’d like to try and arrange accommodation in the hall of residence.
Speaker 1: Officer: Yes. Certainly. Please sit down. What I’ll do is fill in a form with you to find out a little more about your preferences and so forth.
Speaker 2: Student: Thank you.
Speaker 1: Officer: So first of all, can I take your name?
Speaker 2: Student: It’s Anubhat.
Speaker 1: Officer: Could you spell your name, please?
Speaker 2: Student: Yes. A n u b h a, t t.
Speaker 1: Officer: Thanks. And could I ask your date of birth?
Speaker 2: Student: The 03/31/1972.
Speaker 1: Officer: Thank you. And where are you from? Student: India. Officer: Oh, right. And, what will you be studying?
Speaker 2: Student: I’m doing a course in nursing.
Speaker 1: Officer: Right. Thank you. And how long would you want to stay in hall, do you think?
Speaker 2: Student: Well, it would take three years, but I’d only like to stay in hall for two. I’d like to think about living outside for the third year.
Speaker 1: Officer: Fine. And what did you have in mind for catering? Do you want to cook for yourself or have all your meals provided? Student: That that’s full board.
Speaker 2: Is there something in between?
Speaker 1: Officer: Yes. You can just have evening meal provided, which is half board.
Speaker 2: Student: That’s what I’d prefer.
Speaker 1: Officer: Yes. A lot of students opt for that. Now with that in mind, do you have any special diet? Anything we should know about?
Speaker 2: Student: Yes. I don’t take red meat.
Speaker 1: No red meat. Officer: Now thinking about the room itself, we have a number of options. You can have a single study bedroom, or you can have a shared one. These are both what we call simple rooms. The other alternative is to opt for a single bed sit, which actually has more space and better facilities. There’s about 20 a week difference between them.
Speaker 2: Student: Well, actually, my grant is quite generous, and I think the bedsit sounds the best option.
Speaker 1: Officer: Lovely. I’ll put you down for that, and we’ll see what availability is like. Now can I ask some other personal details which we like to have on record?
Speaker 2: Student: Yes. Of course.
Speaker 1: Officer: I wonder if you could let us know what your interests are. This might help us get a closer match for placing you in a particular hall.
Speaker 2: Student: Well, I love the theater.
Speaker 1: Officer: Right.
Speaker 2: Student: And I enjoy sports, particularly badminton.
Speaker 1: Officer: Ah, that’s worth knowing. Now what we finish with on the form is really a list from you of what your priorities are in choosing a hall, and we’ll do our best to take these into account.
Speaker 2: Student: Well, the first thing is I’d prefer a hall where there are other mature students, if possible.
Speaker 1: Officer: Yes. We do have halls which tend to cater for slightly older students.
Speaker 2: Student: And I’d prefer to be out of town.
Speaker 1: Officer: That’s actually very good for you because we tend to have more vacancies in out of town halls.
Speaker 2: Student: Lucky.
Speaker 1: Yes.
Speaker 2: Officer: Anything else? Student: Well, I would like somewhere with a shared area, a a TV room, for example, or or something like that. It’s a good way to socialize.
Speaker 1: Officer: Certainly is.
Speaker 2: That’s it?
Speaker 1: Now we just need a contact telephone number for you.
Speaker 2: Student: Oh, sure. I’ll just find it. It’s 667549.
Speaker 1: Officer: Great. So we’ll be in contact with you as soon as possible.
